title: ​From $2 Trillion to $1.5 Trillion: On the Eve of Anthropic's IPO, Public Markets Pour Cold Water on AI

content_html:
The Wall Street Journal said on Nov. 3 that last week's stampede in tech stocks rewrote the script for Anthropic's IPO valuation. Institutions involved in the IPO are signaling that the valuation at listing by the end of this month should fall between $1.5 trillion and $1.6 trillion, far below the nearly $2 trillion that had been widely discussed.

The trigger was the sharp volatility a week earlier: the Nasdaq fell about 10% from its high, Intel plunged 29% in a single day in its biggest one-day drop in more than 40 years, and Google parent Alphabet lost about $500 billion in market value after earnings. Panic traveled down the chain to this AI star that has yet to ring the opening bell.

The AI narrative faces threefold scrutiny, and pricing becomes a market litmus test

Investor concerns had already spilled beyond the broader market. People familiar with the matter say worries about excessive AI exposure are rising, political resistance to data centers adds another variable, and Amazon, Meta and others still have no timetable for monetizing AI. With doubts piling up, Anthropic's pricing has become a bellwether event for gauging market appetite.

The company has not yet finalized its valuation or the size of its share sale. Some investors expect CFO Rao to price conservatively to ensure first-day buyers see a gain—some judge that even if it opens at $1.5 trillion, its closing market cap could be pushed back to around $2 trillion, just as SpaceX rose 19.22% on its first day and its market cap broke $2.11 trillion. Anthropic could start its roadshow as early as next week, aiming to list before Thanksgiving; its prospectus shows revenue of $17 billion for the quarter ended Sept. 30, up from about $11.6 billion in the previous quarter, but offset by about $600 million in price cuts. As tech stocks enter a "show me the numbers" phase, this IPO tests how well the AI story holds up in the public markets.
